newsitem.title: USA: AMR stock soft ahead of pilot vote results.
newsitem.headline: AMR stock soft ahead of pilot vote results.

text.p: Shares of AMR Corp, the parent of American Airlines, slipped Monday as investors took a cautious stance ahead of the results of American pilots' vote on a tentative labor contract.
"It's market concern ahead of the vote. It's just nervousness, but I expect it will be approved," said Julius Maldutis, an airline analyst with Salomon Brothers.
AMR lost 3-5/8 or almost four percent to 91-1/2. AMR slipped more than the 0.71 percent drop in the Dow Jones transportation average, which lost 18.50 points or 0.71 percent to 2587.33.
The pilots union at American Airlines said it will release the results of the vote Monday after the financial markets close at 1600 EDT/2000 GMT.

Although many analysts and labor experts expect the Allied Pilots Association's 9,300 to approve the proposed five-year pact, investors acted cautiously since the rank-and-file union members have rejected deals in the past.
In January, the APA members rejected a tentative contract despite the union's board recommendation for approval.

When the two sides failed to reach agreement on a new deal, the pilots went on strike on February 15. They were forced back to work within minutes by a Presidential Emergency Board established by President Clinton to resolve the dispute.

In April, the union's 18-member board voted 12 to six to approve the tentative proposal, which marked a compromise on the contentious issue surrounding regional jets to be bought for American's regional carrier, American Eagle.

American had wanted its American Eagle pilots, who are paid less than APA members, to fly smaller jets so the company could remain competitive with low-cost carriers. The APA pilots were concerned that the American Eagle pilots would eventually take over their current routes.
The proposed contract now includes a guarantee that furlouged APA pilots will be able to fly new jets being bought for American Eagle.
The contract includes a nine percent wage increase and 5.75 million stock options valued at $10 below market price.
